title: こぶとりじいさん (The Old Man Who Had His Lump Removed)
description: An old man with a large lump on his cheek shelters from rain in a mountain shrine. Demons emerge and begin dancing wildly; the old man joins in with such joy that the demons take his lump as a pledge for his return. A jealous neighbor with a lump tries the same trick — but the demons, finding him dull, give him the first old man's lump in addition to his own. A classic Japanese folk tale about the difference between genuine joy and greedy imitation.
author: 楠山正雄 (Kusuyama Masao, 1885–1943)
